from stg_order_items_pc i join stg_orders_pc o on o.order_id=i.order_id join stg_products_pc p on p.product_id=i.product_id;
create or replace temp view core_order_items_pc as   -- JNR_ADD_SUPPLY_COST master outer: keep all supply-agg rows
select x.order_item_id, x.order_id, a.product_id, x.ordered_at_day, x.product_name, x.product_type, x.product_price,
       x.is_food_item, x.is_drink_item, coalesce(a.supply_cost_per_product,0) as supply_cost_per_product,
       coalesce(a.has_perishable_supply,0) as has_perishable_supply
from core_supagg a left join core_items_stream x on x.product_id = a.product_id;

create or replace temp view core_supagg2 as select product_id, sum(supply_cost) as scpp_exact, round(sum(supply_cost)) as scpp_round0 from stg_supplies_pc group by 1;
create or replace temp view core_orders_itemagg as
select x.order_id, count(*) as items_count, sum(p.product_price_col) as order_items_subtotal,
       sum(coalesce(a.scpp_exact,0)) as order_cost_exact, sum(coalesce(a.scpp_round0,0)) as order_cost_round0,
       max(p.is_food_item) as has_food, max(p.is_drink_item) as has_drink
from core_supagg2 a left join (stg_order_items_pc x join stg_products_pc p on p.product_id=x.product_id) on x.product_id=a.product_id
group by 1;
create or replace temp view core_orders_pc as
select g.order_id, o.customer_id, o.location_id, o.ordered_at_day,
       o.subtotal_cents_col/100 as subtotal, o.tax_paid_cents_col/100 as tax_paid, o.order_total_cents_col/100 as order_total,
       g.order_items_subtotal, g.order_cost_exact, g.order_cost_round0, g.has_food, g.has_drink,
       row_number() over (order by lower(o.customer_id) nulls first, o.ordered_at_day nulls first, lower(g.order_id) nulls first) as customer_order_number
from core_orders_itemagg g left join stg_orders_pc o on o.order_id = g.order_id;

create or replace temp view core_customers_pc as
select c.customer_id, c.customer_name, a.lifetime_orders, a.first_order_date, a.last_order_date,
       a.lifetime_spend, a.lifetime_spend_pretax, a.lifetime_tax_paid,
       case when coalesce(a.lifetime_orders,0) > 1 then 'returning' else 'new' end as customer_type
from (select customer_id, count(order_id) lifetime_orders, min(ordered_at_day) first_order_date, max(ordered_at_day) last_order_date,
             sum(order_total_col) lifetime_spend, sum(subtotal_col) lifetime_spend_pretax, sum(tax_paid_col) lifetime_tax_paid
      from stg_orders_pc group by 1) a
left join stg_customers_pc c on c.customer_id = a.customer_id;

-- ===== m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED =====
create or replace temp view e_s2 as
select i.order_item_id, i.order_id, i.product_id, o.customer_id, o.location_id, o.ordered_at_day,
       p.product_name, p.product_type, p.product_price_col as product_price, p.is_food_item, p.is_drink_item
from stg_order_items_pc i join stg_orders_pc o on o.order_id=i.order_id join stg_products_pc p on p.product_id=i.product_id;
create or replace temp view e_s3 as  -- JNR_ADD_CUSTOMERS: master=item stream, detail=customers, master outer
select s.order_item_id, s.order_id, s.product_id, s.customer_id, s.location_id, s.ordered_at_day, s.product_name, s.product_type,
       s.product_price, s.is_food_item, s.is_drink_item, c.customer_name
from stg_customers_pc c left join e_s2 s on s.customer_id = c.customer_id;
create or replace temp view e_s4 as  -- JNR_ADD_LOCATIONS
select s.*, l.location_name, l.tax_rate, l.region
from stg_locations_pc l left join e_s3 s on s.location_id = l.location_id;
create or replace temp view e_supagg as select product_id, sum(supply_cost) scpp, max(is_perishable) hps from stg_supplies_pc group by 1;

       coalesce(location_name,'Unknown') location_name, coalesce(region,'Unknown') region, ordered_at_day, product_name, product_type,
       product_price, is_food_item, is_drink_item,
       product_price as item_revenue, coalesce(supply_cost_per_product,0) as item_cogs,
       product_price - coalesce(supply_cost_per_product,0) as item_gross_profit,
       case when product_price = 0 then 0 else (product_price - coalesce(supply_cost_per_product,0))/product_price end as item_gross_margin_pct,
       product_price*coalesce(tax_rate,0) as item_tax_estimate, product_price + product_price*coalesce(tax_rate,0) as item_total_estimate,
       coalesce(has_perishable_supply_in,0) as has_perishable_supply
from e_s5;
create or replace temp view e_itemagg as
select order_id, count(order_item_id) item_lines, sum(item_revenue) item_revenue, sum(item_cogs) order_cogs, sum(item_gross_profit) order_gross_profit,
       sum(is_food_item) food_item_lines, sum(is_drink_item) drink_item_lines
from oie_pc group by 1;
create or replace temp view of_pre as   -- JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG: master=orders, detail=item agg, master outer
select o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.location_id, o.ordered_at_day, o.subtotal_col as order_subtotal, o.tax_paid_col as order_tax_paid,
       o.order_total_col as order_total, coalesce(g.item_lines,0) item_lines, coalesce(g.item_revenue,0) item_revenue,
       coalesce(g.order_cogs,0) order_cogs, coalesce(g.order_gross_profit,0) order_gross_profit,
       case when coalesce(g.item_revenue,0)=0 then 0 else coalesce(g.order_gross_profit,0)/g.item_revenue end order_gross_margin_pct,
       case when o.subtotal_col = 0 then 0 else o.tax_paid_col/o.subtotal_col end effective_tax_rate,
       coalesce(g.food_item_lines,0) food_item_lines, coalesce(g.drink_item_lines,0) drink_item_lines
from e_itemagg g left join stg_orders_pc o on o.order_id = g.order_id;
create or replace temp view of_pc as
select *, row_number() over (order by lower(customer_id), ordered_at_day, lower(order_id)) as customer_order_number,
       case when order_total >= 50 then 'HIGH' when order_total < 50 then 'STANDARD' end as order_value_band
from of_pre where order_total is not null;   -- router default group unconnected
create or replace temp view c360_agg as
select customer_id, count(order_id) cnt, min(ordered_at_day) first_at, max(ordered_at_day) last_at, sum(order_total) spend,

       sum(case when order_value_band='HIGH' then 1 else 0 end) high
from of_pc group by 1;
create or replace temp view c360_pc as
select a.customer_id, c.customer_name, a.cnt, a.first_at, a.last_at, a.spend, a.pretax, a.tax, a.cogs, a.gp, a.high,
       date_diff('day', a.last_at, date '2025-12-31') as recency_days
from c360_agg a left join stg_customers_pc c on c.customer_id = a.customer_id;
EOF

# Blind review: FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml

Independent, from-scratch review of `external/flowline-pwc-demo/FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml` (4,701 lines) before writing a PowerCenter-to-dbt converter.

## How this was done

- **XML.** Read through a redacting parser (VALUEPAIR attributes dropped). The compact dumps and wiring checks are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-junaidatique--claude-spares-spare-x2tKTE/df021aa3-23ff-4dbf-a7c9-3e227d3a8b25/scratchpad/review/blind/work/` (`maps.txt`, `wiring.txt`, `outline.txt`). Every line number below was checked against the raw file. "L" means physical line in the XML.
- **Intent.** dbt-labs/jaffle-shop models (`models/staging`, `models/marts`). The jaffle-shop dbt outputs that are already built in the same DuckDB file (`main.orders`, `main.customers`, `main.order_items`, …) serve as the "intended" values.
- **Data impact.** I simulated what PowerCenter would actually do on the seed (`raw.*`). The view definitions are in `work/sim.sql`; `work/run.py` attaches the seed read-only and runs them; the raw query output is in `work/impact1.txt` … `impact4.txt`. The simulation follows PowerCenter semantics: joiner master/detail roles, port order, the unconnected router default group, and the 'True'/'False' text that the source DDL implies for `PERISHABLE`.
- **Seed facts used throughout.** 935 customers (all have orders), 61,948 orders (2024-09-01 to 2025-08-31), 483 of those orders have no items (all with subtotal/tax/total 0, belonging to 85 customers), 90,900 items, 10 products (all sold, all have supplies), 65 supply rows (29 distinct supply ids), 6 stores (only Philadelphia and Brooklyn have orders).

Categories: **wrong data**, **misleading-but-works**, **harmless**, **security**. Confidence: **confirmed** (evidence in the XML plus documented PowerCenter semantics, and measured where possible), **likely**, **speculative**.

## Summary

| ID | Title | Category | Confidence | Seed impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F01 | STG_ORDERS cents and dollars columns cross-wired | wrong data | confirmed | 61,465 / 61,948 rows; every downstream order amount |
| F02 | STG_PRODUCTS price and price-cents cross-wired | wrong data | confirmed | 10 / 10 products; every price, revenue, margin |
| F03 | Core ORDERS re-derives dollars from columns that already hold dollars (÷10,000 overall) | wrong data | confirmed | 61,465 / 61,465 rows |
| F04 | Revenue (cents) minus cost (dollars): every gross-profit and margin metric is wrong | wrong data | confirmed | all item, order, product-day and store-day margins ≈0.998 instead of ≈0.79 |
| F05 | CUSTOMER_360 LIFETIME_SPEND / _PRETAX / _TAX_PAID rotated | wrong data | confirmed | 935 / 935 rows |
| F06 | PRODUCT_DAILY_PERFORMANCE MARGIN_PCT and PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG swapped (with rounding into NUMBER(1,0)) | wrong data | confirmed | 3,635 / 3,635 rows |
| F07 | CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUMBER is a global running number (variable-port order bug), in core and enriched | wrong data | confirmed | 61,275 / 61,465 rows differ from intent |
| F08 | STORE_DAILY_KPIS.UNIQUE_CUSTOMERS is always 0 (same bug) | wrong data | confirmed | 538 / 538 store-days |
| F09 | ORDER_VALUE_BAND threshold of 50 is compared against cents, so 100 % of orders are HIGH | wrong data | confirmed | 61,465 HIGH vs 1,216 intended |
| F10 | Orders without items dropped by the Master Outer joins (core ORDERS, enriched ORDER_FINANCIALS and everything downstream) | wrong data | confirmed | 483 orders; 85 customers; 319 store-days |
| F11 | Master/detail roles inverted on every Master Outer join (systemic, mostly latent) | wrong data (latent) | confirmed | 0 extra rows on seed beyond F10 |
| F12 | M_SCORE thresholds compared against cents | wrong data | confirmed | M=3 for 935 / 935 (intended 797/112/26) |
| F13 | $$RUN_DATE is a fixed 2025-12-31 default, the parameter file is not in the export, the workflow variable is unused | misleading-but-works | confirmed (effective value unknown) | R_SCORE = 1 for all 935 |
| F14 | RFM 'PROSPECT' (and the ISNULL cleanup) is unreachable | misleading-but-works | confirmed | 0 PROSPECT |
| F15 | IS_PERISHABLE only recognises 'Y'/'1', but the source is varchar2 holding CSV booleans | wrong data | likely | 30 / 65 supplies, all 10 products, all 90,900 items flagged 0 |
| F16 | Scale-0 decimal ports on money (core supply cost, order cost, store gross profit) | misleading / latent | speculative (impact) | 0 under current settings; 61,377 orders would change if high precision were on |
| F17 | ORDERED_AT_DAY built with TO_CHAR/TO_DATE 'DD-MM-YY' (two-digit year) | misleading-but-works | likely | 0 rows |
| F18 | ERROR() defaults on two I/O ports drop NULL rows; output-port defaults of '0' do not replace NULLs | misleading-but-works | likely | 0 rows |
| F19 | REGION from tax-rate bands: all stores are AMER; the router/sorter/union chain is a no-op; port-suffix traps | harmless | confirmed | all 6 stores AMER |
| F20 | Staging inner-joins supplies to products; STG_SUPPLIES has no unique key | harmless | confirmed | 0 rows dropped |
| F21 | Food/drink flags are case-insensitive and trimmed (jaffle-shop compares exactly) | harmless | confirmed | 0 rows |
| F22 | Rows with NULL ORDER_TOTAL fall into the unconnected router DEFAULT group | harmless | confirmed | 0 rows |
| F23 | Duplicated logic (two supply aggregators, two recency expressions, separate order-item pipelines) | misleading-but-works | confirmed | feeds F16 |
| F24 | Cross-mapping inconsistencies between core and enriched marts | wrong data | confirmed | see table |
| F25 | Unconditional workflow links and swallowed failures: marts rebuild even if staging fails | wrong data (operational) | confirmed (config) / speculative (impact) | not measurable |
| F26 | Reusable staging session points at MART_Jaffleshop; only the workflow task instance points it at RAW_/STG_ | misleading-but-works | confirmed | none when run via the workflow |
| F27 | Plaintext credential in Command task `cmd_FL_JS_CREATE_RPT_VIEWS` | security | confirmed | n/a |

---

## Findings

### F01: STG_ORDERS cents and dollars columns cross-wired
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** EXP_ORDERS L106–125 (L111–116); connectors L608–613; STG_ORDERS target L67–78.

- **Lines:** EXP_RFM_SEGMENT L2366 (`IIF(COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS=0,'PROSPECT', …`); EXP_CUSTOMER_METRICS L2256 (`COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS` = `COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS_IN`, not the cleaned `v_ORDERS_CL` at L2267); JNR_CUSTOMERS L2227–2252.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:**
  1. JNR_CUSTOMERS keeps only customers that have orders (F11).
  2. Even if a no-order customer got through, COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS would be NULL, not 0. `NULL = 0` is NULL and IIF falls through, so the customer would end up STANDARD (R=1 via 9999 days, F=1, M=1) and be written with a NULL order count.
  3. The `IIF(ISNULL(...),0,...)` cleanups at L2267–2273 never fire.
- **Seed impact:** 0 PROSPECT rows (and 0 customers without orders in the seed).
- **dbt translation:** keep the logic as written but document it as dead code. If the joins are fixed (F11), this branch still needs `coalesce(count,0)` to work.

### F15: IS_PERISHABLE only recognises 'Y'/'1', but the source is varchar2 holding CSV booleans
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** likely, because it depends on how RAW_SUPPLIES was loaded into Oracle.
- **Lines:** source RAW_SUPPLIES.PERISHABLE L10 (`varchar2`, precision 50); EXP_SUPPLIES L504 `IIF(PERISHABLE = 'Y' OR PERISHABLE = '1', 1, 0)` (default '0'); aggregated by L1444 and L3292 `MAX(IS_PERISHABLE)`; consumers L1507, L2159, L3340.
- **Evidence:** the jaffle-shop seed file `raw_supplies.csv` stores `perishable` as `True`/`False`, and DuckDB loads it as BOOLEAN. A varchar2 column loaded from that file holds 'True'/'False'. The comparison is case-sensitive and exact. NULL also gives 0.
- **Seed impact (if stored as 'True'/'False'):**
  - IS_PERISHABLE = 0 for 65 / 65 supplies (30 should be 1);
  - HAS_PERISHABLE_SUPPLY = 0 for all 10 products and all 90,900 items in core ORDER_ITEMS and ORDER_ITEM_ENRICHED (every product actually has a perishable supply);
  - PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG = 0 (before the F06 swap).
  ```sql
  select count(*) filter (where is_perishable=1), count(*) from stg_supplies_pc;              -- 0, 65
  select count(*) filter (where is_perishable_supply) from seed.main.stg_supplies;             -- 30
  ```
- **dbt translation:** faithful: `case when perishable in ('Y','1') then 1 else 0 end` on the text value. When loading a boolean seed into a DuckDB/dbt target, cast to the same text the Oracle table holds, otherwise the result silently changes. Intended: jaffle-shop `perishable as is_perishable_supply`.

### F16: Scale-0 decimal ports on money values
- **Category:** misleading / latent. **Confidence:** the type facts are confirmed; the rounding impact is speculative.
- **Lines:**
  - core AGG_SUPPLIES_BY_PRODUCT2 L3382 `SUM(SUPPLY_COST)` as decimal(10,0), carried through JNR L3441 → AGG_ITEMS_BY_ORDER input L3465 decimal(12,0) → ORDER_COST L3460 decimal(12,0) and ORDER_ITEMS_SUBTOTAL L3459 decimal(12,0) → EXP_ORDERS_CALC L3537–3538 (12,0) → ORDERS NUMBER(12,2);
  - enriched AGG_BY_LOCATION_DAY GROSS_PROFIT_TOTAL L2009 decimal(12,0) → EXP_STORE_KPIS L2036 decimal(12,2);
  - staging EXP_ORDERS ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS L116 decimal(12,0);
  - the sibling aggregator for ORDER_ITEMS is decimal(12,2) at L3291;
  - all three sessions have "Enable high precision" = NO (L1007, L4292, L4570).
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** with high precision off, decimal ports are processed as double. I expect the port scale not to be applied, so values are probably not rounded, but I cannot prove this from the XML. With high precision on, these ports round to whole units.
- **Seed impact:**
  - If no rounding: core ORDERS.ORDER_COST matches jaffle-shop exactly (0 diffs).
  - If rounding: 61,377 / 61,465 orders change and the ORDER_COST total becomes 151,444 instead of 131,788.38.
  - GROSS_PROFIT_TOTAL would change on all 538 store-days (by less than one unit).
  - ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS: no impact (the seed holds integer cents).
  ```sql
  select count(*) filter (where round(p.order_cost_exact,2) <> j.order_cost), count(*) filter (where p.order_cost_round0 <> j.order_cost),
         sum(j.order_cost), sum(p.order_cost_round0) from core_orders_pc p join seed.main.orders j using(order_id);  -- 0, 61377, 131788.38, 151444
  ```
- **dbt translation:** the converter must decide how to map decimal(p,0) under high precision NO; recommend double (no rounding) and record it as an assumption. Two other points to flag: the core ORDERS supply cost is computed separately from ORDER_ITEMS at lower precision (F23), and the enriched store gross-profit total is typed as an integer.

### F17: ORDERED_AT_DAY via TO_CHAR/TO_DATE with a two-digit year
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** likely (century rule); the zero seed impact is confirmed.
- **Lines:** EXP_ORDERS L110 `TO_DATE(TO_CHAR(ORDERED_AT, 'DD-MM-YY'), 'DD-MM-YY')`.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:**
  - The round trip drops the time of day (the intent is `date_trunc('day')`, as in jaffle-shop `stg_orders`).
  - With `YY`, TO_DATE assumes the current century, so a 1999 timestamp would come back as 2099. `RR`, or simply `TRUNC(ORDERED_AT)` as used for locations at L234, would avoid that.
  - A NULL timestamp stays NULL.
- **Seed impact:** 0 of 61,948. All years are 2024–2025.
- **dbt translation:** `date_trunc('day', ordered_at)`. Note the century caveat if historical data could predate 2000.

### F18: ERROR() defaults on two I/O ports drop NULL rows; output-port defaults do not replace NULLs
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** likely.
- **Lines:**
  - EXP_LOCATIONS.TAX_RATE L235: INPUT/OUTPUT with default `ERROR('Transformation Error')`;
  - EXP_ORDER_ITEMS.ORDER_ID L455: INPUT/OUTPUT with the same default;
  - EXP_SUPPLIES L503 `SUPPLY_COST` (OUTPUT, default '0') and L504 `IS_PERISHABLE` (OUTPUT, default '0');
  - "Stop on errors" 0 at L793.
- **Evidence:** every other I/O port in the file has an empty default (system default NULL).
- **PowerCenter reasoning:**
  - On input and I/O ports, the default value replaces a NULL input. ERROR() skips the row with a row error. "Stop on errors" = 0 means unlimited errors, so the row silently disappears from STG_LOCATIONS or STG_ORDER_ITEMS.
  - On output ports, defaults apply only to transformation errors. A NULL COST still gives a NULL SUPPLY_COST, not 0.
- **Seed impact:** 0. There are no NULL tax rates and no NULL item order_ids.
- **dbt translation:** faithful: `where tax_rate is not null` for STG_LOCATIONS and `where order_id is not null` for STG_ORDER_ITEMS. Ideally log what was dropped. Do **not** add `coalesce(...,0)` for the output-port defaults.

### F19: REGION from tax-rate bands; the router/sorter/union chain is a no-op; port-suffix traps
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** EXP_LOCATIONS L236; SRT_LOC_BEFORE L258–273; RTR_REGION L274–306 (groups L276–279, DEFAULT1 L277, outputs L300–304 unconnected); SRT_APAC/AMER/EMEA L307–354; EXP_*_RENAME_TRANS L355–367, L427–452; UN_REGIONS L368–426; SRT_LOC_AFTER L242–257.

- **Seed impact:** every one of the 6 stores (tax 0.04–0.08) gets REGION = 'AMER'. The APAC and EMEA paths carry no rows. STG_LOCATIONS keeps all 6 rows.
- **Converter trap:** suffix numbers do not line up between transformations, so follow connectors, not names:
  - router `*2` ports are the DEFAULT group, while union `*2` ports are the APAC input;
  - in the enriched mapping, router `*2` is DEFAULT while union `*2` is the HIGH input (L1797–1814 vs L1884–1902).

### F20: Staging inner-joins supplies to products; STG_SUPPLIES has no unique key
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** JNR_SUPPLIES_PRODUCTS L479–498 (L488 `SKU1 = SKU`, L489 `Normal Join`, master SKU1 L485 fed by SQ_RAW_PRODUCTS1 L756); STG_SUPPLIES target L44–51.

- **Seed impact:** 0 supplies dropped. 65 rows, 29 distinct supply ids.

### F21: Food/drink flags are case-insensitive and trimmed
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** EXP_PRODUCTS L204–205 `IIF( UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(TYPE))) = 'JAFFLE', 1, 0 )` (likewise 'BEVERAGE').
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** NULL TYPE gives 0, which matches jaffle-shop's `coalesce(type='jaffle', false)`. The only difference is case and whitespace tolerance.
- **Seed impact:** 0 (types are exactly 'jaffle' and 'beverage').
- **dbt translation:** `case when upper(trim(type)) = 'JAFFLE' then 1 else 0 end`.

### F22: Rows with NULL ORDER_TOTAL fall into the unconnected router DEFAULT group
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** RTR_ORDER_VALUE_BAND L1741 (DEFAULT1), outputs L1797–1814 (no connectors).
- **PowerCenter reasoning:**
  - NULL ≥ 50 and NULL < 50 are both NULL, i.e. false, so the row goes to DEFAULT1 and is lost. This can only happen for an item-aggregate row with no matching order: F11, the master-side ORDER_TOTAL is NULL.
  - The two conditions do not overlap and leave no gap apart from NULL.
- **Seed impact:** 0.
- **dbt translation:** `where order_total is not null` before banding.

### F23: Duplicated logic
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:**
  - core AGG_SUPPLIES_BY_PRODUCT L3287–3302 (decimal(12,2)) vs AGG_SUPPLIES_BY_PRODUCT2 L3380–3391 (decimal(10,0)), both summing STG_SUPPLIES.SUPPLY_COST by product;

### F24: Cross-mapping inconsistencies between core and enriched marts
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** confirmed.

| Metric | Core (mapping, lines) | Enriched (mapping, lines) | Seed result |

### F25: Unconditional workflow links and swallowed failures
- **Category:** wrong data (operational). **Confidence:** the configuration is confirmed; the impact is speculative.
- **Lines:**
  - WORKFLOWLINK L4622–4625, all with `CONDITION =""`;
  - TASKINSTANCE L4577, L4579, L4620 and L4621 with `FAIL_PARENT_IF_INSTANCE_FAILS ="NO"`;

  - "Stop on errors" 0 (L793);
  - "Rollback Transactions on Errors" NO (L999, L4284, L4562);

  - workflow SUSPEND_ON_ERROR NO (L4054);
  - Pre-SQL TRUNCATE on every target: L535–550, L2389–2401, L3691–3703.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:**
  - An empty link condition means the next task starts whatever the previous task's status.
  - If staging fails after its Pre-SQL truncation, core and enriched still truncate and rebuild the marts from empty or partial STG tables.
  - The workflow is not marked failed.
  - Row-level errors (F06 overflow, F18 NULLs) are dropped without failing anything.
- **Seed impact:** not measurable from a static run.
- **dbt translation:** dbt's DAG stops downstream models on failure, which is a behaviour change worth calling out. Do not try to reproduce "continue on failure".

### F26: Reusable staging session vs workflow task-instance connection overrides
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:**
  - Reusable `s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL` L811–1013: every reader and writer uses `MART_Jaffleshop` (e.g. L888, L900, L912, L961, L965 …).

- **PowerCenter reasoning:** task-instance overrides win, so the workflow run behaves correctly. Run on its own, the reusable session would read RAW_* and write STG_* through the MART connection.
- **Seed impact:** none via the workflow.
- **dbt translation:** a converter must resolve connections as task-instance override, then session, then mapping. Map RAW/STG/MART to dbt sources and schemas accordingly.

### F27: Plaintext credential in Command task `cmd_FL_JS_CREATE_RPT_VIEWS`
- **Category:** security. **Confidence:** confirmed.

- **Evidence:** the task contains a plaintext database credential. Its content is deliberately not reproduced or described here.
- **Impact:** anyone with access to the export (or to the repository it is committed in) has the credential. The reporting views this task creates are not visible to the mappings, so they cannot be checked or converted from the XML.
- **dbt translation:** do not port the command or copy the credential. Treat the credential as compromised and rotate it. If the report views are needed, rebuild them as dbt models (or post-hooks) that use profile-managed credentials.

---

## Intent differences vs jaffle-shop (by design, not defects)
- There is no LOCATIONS mart (only STG_LOCATIONS); jaffle-shop has `locations`.
- ORDERS has HAS_FOOD_ITEMS / HAS_DRINK_ITEMS (MAX of flags) instead of jaffle-shop's `count_food_items`, `count_drink_items`, `count_order_items`, `is_food_order`, `is_drink_order`. ITEMS_COUNT is computed (L3458) but never written.
- STG_SUPPLIES has no `supply_uuid`. STG_PRODUCTS and PRODUCTS add `PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS`.
- The enriched marts (ORDER_ITEM_ENRICHED, ORDER_FINANCIALS, CUSTOMER_360, PRODUCT_DAILY_PERFORMANCE, STORE_DAILY_KPIS) have no jaffle-shop equivalent; their intent was inferred from names and formulas.

## Areas checked and found clean
- **Connector integrity:** every connector references an existing port. No port is fed twice. Every transformation input and every target column is connected. Mapping wiring was checked across all 28 source qualifiers, 25 expressions, 16 joiners, 9 aggregators, 15 sorters, 2 routers, 2 unions and 1 filter (`work/wiring.txt`).
- **String precision:** no string narrowing along any connector or into any target. Seed maximum lengths fit the declared precisions (names ≤ 32, descriptions ≤ 94, ids ≤ 36).
- **Source qualifiers:** none has a SQL override, user-defined join, source filter, sorted ports, Select Distinct or pre/post SQL. No session-level transformation overrides exist.
- **Aggregators:** every output port is either a group-by port or an aggregate. No non-aggregated outputs. Unused inputs (e.g. CUSTOMER_ID at L2012, SUPPLY_ID/SUPPLY_NAME at L3288–3289) are input-only, so harmless. COUNT(*) at L3458 is valid. Sorted Input is NO everywhere, so there is no dependency on sorter output.
- **Sorters:** no Distinct. Only the two sequence expressions (F07, F08) depend on sort order, and their sort keys match their intent. Case-insensitive sorting has no effect on lower-case UUID keys.
- **Joiner keys:** string-to-string everywhere. Case-sensitive comparison matches SQL. The inner (Normal) joins (staging supplies↔products, items↔orders, items↔products) are correct apart from F20.
- **Other expressions:** TRUNC(OPENED_AT) (L234), EFFECTIVE_TAX_RATE and food/drink shares, all ISNULL cleanups and IIF guards against division by zero. There is no integer division anywhere (every division involves a decimal or double).
- **Unions:** both act as UNION ALL, input groups align with their sources via the connectors, and all 19 + 19 (enriched) and 15 (staging) inputs are connected.
- **Filter FIL_LOCS:** correct for what it does (see F11).
- **Target load order** (L762–767, L3099–3103, L4047–4051): the pipelines inside each mapping are independent, so order does not matter. **Pre-SQL truncation plus bulk insert** is a valid full refresh (risk only as in F25).
- **Session date format** (L782) is consistent with the `$$RUN_DATE` default format. There are no mapplets, shortcuts, worklets, lookups, update strategies or sequence generators.

Independent, from-scratch review of `external/flowline-pwc-demo/FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml` (4,701 lines) before writing a PowerCenter-to-dbt converter.

## How this was done

- **XML.** Read through a redacting parser (VALUEPAIR attributes dropped). The compact dumps and wiring checks are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-junaidatique--claude-spares-spare-x2tKTE/df021aa3-23ff-4dbf-a7c9-3e227d3a8b25/scratchpad/review/blind/work/` (`maps.txt`, `wiring.txt`, `outline.txt`). Every line number below was checked against the raw file. "L" means physical line in the XML.
- **Intent.** dbt-labs/jaffle-shop models (`models/staging`, `models/marts`). The jaffle-shop dbt outputs that are already built in the same DuckDB file (`main.orders`, `main.customers`, `main.order_items`, …) serve as the "intended" values.

The view definitions are in `work/sim.sql`; `work/run.py` attaches the seed read-only and runs them; the raw query output is in `work/impact1.txt` … `impact4.txt`. ## Findings

### F01: STG_ORDERS cents and dollars columns cross-wired
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** confirmed.

- **Evidence:**
  - `EXP_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL` = `SUBTOTAL_IN/100` (L111). `SUBTOTAL_CENTS` = `SUBTOTAL_IN` (L114). The same pattern holds for TAX_PAID (L112/L115) and ORDER_TOTAL (L113/L116).

- **PowerCenter reasoning:** connectors are explicit, by name. Target columns receive exactly what is wired, whatever the column name. So `STG_ORDERS.*_CENTS` hold dollars and `STG_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL/TAX_PAID/ORDER_TOTAL` hold cents.

- **dbt translation:** keep the logic as written but document it as dead code. If the joins are fixed (F11), this branch still needs `coalesce(count,0)` to work.

### F15: IS_PERISHABLE only recognises 'Y'/'1', but the source is varchar2 holding CSV booleans
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** likely, because it depends on how RAW_SUPPLIES was loaded into Oracle.
- **Lines:** source RAW_SUPPLIES.PERISHABLE L10 (`varchar2`, precision 50); EXP_SUPPLIES L504 `IIF(PERISHABLE = 'Y' OR PERISHABLE = '1', 1, 0)` (default '0'); aggregated by L1444 and L3292 `MAX(IS_PERISHABLE)`; consumers L1507, L2159, L3340.
- **Evidence:** the jaffle-shop seed file `raw_supplies.csv` stores `perishable` as `True`/`False`, and DuckDB loads it as BOOLEAN. A varchar2 column loaded from that file holds 'True'/'False'. The comparison is case-sensitive and exact. NULL also gives 0.
- **Seed impact (if stored as 'True'/'False'):**
  - IS_PERISHABLE = 0 for 65 / 65 supplies (30 should be 1);
  - HAS_PERISHABLE_SUPPLY = 0 for all 10 products and all 90,900 items in core ORDER_ITEMS and ORDER_ITEM_ENRICHED (every product actually has a perishable supply);
  - PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG = 0 (before the F06 swap).
  ```sql
  select count(*) filter (where is_perishable=1), count(*) from stg_supplies_pc;              -- 0, 65
  select count(*) filter (where is_perishable_supply) from seed.main.stg_supplies;             -- 30
  ```
- **dbt translation:** faithful: `case when perishable in ('Y','1') then 1 else 0 end` on the text value. When loading a boolean seed into a DuckDB/dbt target, cast to the same text the Oracle table holds, otherwise the result silently changes. Intended: jaffle-shop `perishable as is_perishable_supply`.

### F16: Scale-0 decimal ports on money values
- **Category:** misleading / latent. **Confidence:** the type facts are confirmed; the rounding impact is speculative.
- **Lines:**
  - core AGG_SUPPLIES_BY_PRODUCT2 L3382 `SUM(SUPPLY_COST)` as decimal(10,0), carried through JNR L3441 → AGG_ITEMS_BY_ORDER input L3465 decimal(12,0) → ORDER_COST L3460 decimal(12,0) and ORDER_ITEMS_SUBTOTAL L3459 decimal(12,0) → EXP_ORDERS_CALC L3537–3538 (12,0) → ORDERS NUMBER(12,2);
  - enriched AGG_BY_LOCATION_DAY GROSS_PROFIT_TOTAL L2009 decimal(12,0) → EXP_STORE_KPIS L2036 decimal(12,2);
  - staging EXP_ORDERS ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS L116 decimal(12,0);
  - the sibling aggregator for ORDER_ITEMS is decimal(12,2) at L3291;
  - all three sessions have "Enable high precision" = NO (L1007, L4292, L4570).
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** with high precision off, decimal ports are processed as double. I expect the port scale not to be applied, so values are probably not rounded, but I cannot prove this from the XML. With high precision on, these ports round to whole units.
- **Seed impact:**
  - If no rounding: core ORDERS.ORDER_COST matches jaffle-shop exactly (0 diffs).
  - If rounding: 61,377 / 61,465 orders change and the ORDER_COST total becomes 151,444 instead of 131,788.38.
  - GROSS_PROFIT_TOTAL would change on all 538 store-days (by less than one unit).
  - ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS: no impact (the seed holds integer cents).
  ```sql
  select count(*) filter (where round(p.order_cost_exact,2) <> j.order_cost), count(*) filter (where p.order_cost_round0 <> j.order_cost),
         sum(j.order_cost), sum(p.order_cost_round0) from core_orders_pc p join seed.main.orders j using(order_id);  -- 0, 61377, 131788.38, 151444
  ```
- **dbt translation:** the converter must decide how to map decimal(p,0) under high precision NO; recommend double (no rounding) and record it as an assumption. Two other points to flag: the core ORDERS supply cost is computed separately from ORDER_ITEMS at lower precision (F23), and the enriched store gross-profit total is typed as an integer.

### F17: ORDERED_AT_DAY via TO_CHAR/TO_DATE with a two-digit year
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** likely (century rule); the zero seed impact is confirmed.
- **Lines:** EXP_ORDERS L110 `TO_DATE(TO_CHAR(ORDERED_AT, 'DD-MM-YY'), 'DD-MM-YY')`.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:**
  - The round trip drops the time of day (the intent is `date_trunc('day')`, as in jaffle-shop `stg_orders`).
  - With `YY`, TO_DATE assumes the current century, so a 1999 timestamp would come back as 2099. `RR`, or simply `TRUNC(ORDERED_AT)` as used for locations at L234, would avoid that.
  - A NULL timestamp stays NULL.
- **Seed impact:** 0 of 61,948. All years are 2024–2025.
- **dbt translation:** `date_trunc('day', ordered_at)`. Note the century caveat if historical data could predate 2000.

### F18: ERROR() defaults on two I/O ports drop NULL rows; output-port defaults do not replace NULLs
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** likely.
- **Lines:**
  - EXP_LOCATIONS.TAX_RATE L235: INPUT/OUTPUT with default `ERROR('Transformation Error')`;
  - EXP_ORDER_ITEMS.ORDER_ID L455: INPUT/OUTPUT with the same default;
  - EXP_SUPPLIES L503 `SUPPLY_COST` (OUTPUT, default '0') and L504 `IS_PERISHABLE` (OUTPUT, default '0');
  - "Stop on errors" 0 at L793.
- **Evidence:** every other I/O port in the file has an empty default (system default NULL).
- **PowerCenter reasoning:**
  - On input and I/O ports, the default value replaces a NULL input. ERROR() skips the row with a row error. "Stop on errors" = 0 means unlimited errors, so the row silently disappears from STG_LOCATIONS or STG_ORDER_ITEMS.
  - On output ports, defaults apply only to transformation errors. A NULL COST still gives a NULL SUPPLY_COST, not 0.
- **Seed impact:** 0. There are no NULL tax rates and no NULL item order_ids.
- **dbt translation:** faithful: `where tax_rate is not null` for STG_LOCATIONS and `where order_id is not null` for STG_ORDER_ITEMS. Ideally log what was dropped. Do **not** add `coalesce(...,0)` for the output-port defaults.

### F19: REGION from tax-rate bands; the router/sorter/union chain is a no-op; port-suffix traps
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** EXP_LOCATIONS L236; SRT_LOC_BEFORE L258–273; RTR_REGION L274–306 (groups L276–279, DEFAULT1 L277, outputs L300–304 unconnected); SRT_APAC/AMER/EMEA L307–354; EXP_*_RENAME_TRANS L355–367, L427–452; UN_REGIONS L368–426; SRT_LOC_AFTER L242–257.
- **Evidence:** `IIF(TAX_RATE >= 0.15,'EMEA', IIF(TAX_RATE >= 0.09,'APAC','AMER'))`. The G_APAC expression has a trailing CR/LF. All three branches are unioned straight back together and re-sorted, and none of it is in jaffle-shop.
- **Seed impact:** every one of the 6 stores (tax 0.04–0.08) gets REGION = 'AMER'. The APAC and EMEA paths carry no rows. STG_LOCATIONS keeps all 6 rows.
- **Converter trap:** suffix numbers do not line up between transformations, so follow connectors, not names:
  - router `*2` ports are the DEFAULT group, while union `*2` ports are the APAC input;
  - in the enriched mapping, router `*2` is DEFAULT while union `*2` is the HIGH input (L1797–1814 vs L1884–1902).
- **dbt translation:** a single `case` expression; drop the sorts and the union.

### F20: Staging inner-joins supplies to products; STG_SUPPLIES has no unique key
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** JNR_SUPPLIES_PRODUCTS L479–498 (L488 `SKU1 = SKU`, L489 `Normal Join`, master SKU1 L485 fed by SQ_RAW_PRODUCTS1 L756); STG_SUPPLIES target L44–51.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** a Normal join drops supplies whose SKU is not in RAW_PRODUCTS. jaffle-shop does not filter supplies. STG_SUPPLIES/SUPPLIES have no `supply_uuid`, and SUPPLY_ID is not unique.
- **Seed impact:** 0 supplies dropped. 65 rows, 29 distinct supply ids.
- **dbt translation:** an inner join to products; do not put a uniqueness test on supply_id.

### F21: Food/drink flags are case-insensitive and trimmed
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** EXP_PRODUCTS L204–205 `IIF( UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(TYPE))) = 'JAFFLE', 1, 0 )` (likewise 'BEVERAGE').
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** NULL TYPE gives 0, which matches jaffle-shop's `coalesce(type='jaffle', false)`. The only difference is case and whitespace tolerance.
- **Seed impact:** 0 (types are exactly 'jaffle' and 'beverage').
- **dbt translation:** `case when upper(trim(type)) = 'JAFFLE' then 1 else 0 end`.

### F22: Rows with NULL ORDER_TOTAL fall into the unconnected router DEFAULT group
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** RTR_ORDER_VALUE_BAND L1741 (DEFAULT1), outputs L1797–1814 (no connectors).
- **PowerCenter reasoning:**
  - NULL ≥ 50 and NULL < 50 are both NULL, i.e. false, so the row goes to DEFAULT1 and is lost. This can only happen for an item-aggregate row with no matching order: F11, the master-side ORDER_TOTAL is NULL.
  - The two conditions do not overlap and leave no gap apart from NULL.
- **Seed impact:** 0.
- **dbt translation:** `where order_total is not null` before banding.

### F23: Duplicated logic
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:**
  - core AGG_SUPPLIES_BY_PRODUCT L3287–3302 (decimal(12,2)) vs AGG_SUPPLIES_BY_PRODUCT2 L3380–3391 (decimal(10,0)), both summing STG_SUPPLIES.SUPPLY_COST by product;
  - core ORDERS rebuilds its own item pipeline (SQ_STG_ORDER_ITEMS1, SQ_STG_PRODUCTS2, SQ_STG_SUPPLIES2, L3345–3455) instead of aggregating ORDER_ITEMS as jaffle-shop does;
  - EXP_RECENCY1 L2300 and EXP_RECENCY2 L2318 compute the same expression, and EXP_RECENCY2's input RECENCY_DAYS_TEMP (L2319) is unused;
  - STG_ORDERS, STG_PRODUCTS, STG_SUPPLIES, STG_CUSTOMERS and STG_LOCATIONS are each read 2–3 times.
- **Seed impact:** none by itself; it feeds F16.
- **dbt translation:** collapse into one CTE or ref each. Keep the precision difference only if reproducing F16.

### F24: Cross-mapping inconsistencies between core and enriched marts
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** confirmed.

| Metric | Core (mapping, lines) | Enriched (mapping, lines) | Seed result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Order total / subtotal / tax | ORDERS = raw ÷ 10,000 (F03, L3534–3536) | ORDER_FINANCIALS = raw cents (F01, L2740–2742) | differ by ×10,000 on 61,465 orders |
| Lifetime spend | CUSTOMERS.LIFETIME_SPEND = Σ cents (L3636) | CUSTOMER_360.LIFETIME_SPEND = Σ tax cents (F05) | differ on 935 / 935 |
| Lifetime order count | CUSTOMERS from all STG orders (L4022–4027) | CUSTOMER_360 from orders with items only (F10) | 85 customers differ |
| First/last order date | CUSTOMERS (L3634–3635) | CUSTOMER_360 (L2188–2189) | 5 customers differ on each |
| Order count | ORDERS 61,465 rows | ORDER_FINANCIALS 61,465 rows | equal to each other, both 483 short of jaffle-shop |
| Supply cost per product | ORDER_ITEMS decimal(12,2) L3291; ORDERS via decimal(10,0) L3382 | ITEM_COGS decimal(12,2) L1443 | equal unless scale is enforced (F16) |
| Margin denominator | — | ORDER_FINANCIALS uses ITEM_REVENUE (L1613), STORE_DAILY_KPIS uses SUBTOTAL_TOTAL (L2038), PRODUCT uses REVENUE (L2182) | equal on seed (order subtotal = item subtotal for all 61,465 orders) |
| CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUMBER | global sequence (F07) | global sequence (F07) | identical to each other, both wrong |

- **dbt translation:** whether a faithful port reproduces these differences or one shared model replaces them is a product decision. Either way, document it.

### F25: Unconditional workflow links and swallowed failures
- **Category:** wrong data (operational). **Confidence:** the configuration is confirmed; the impact is speculative.
- **Lines:**
  - WORKFLOWLINK L4622–4625, all with `CONDITION =""`;
  - TASKINSTANCE L4577, L4579, L4620 and L4621 with `FAIL_PARENT_IF_INSTANCE_FAILS ="NO"`;
  - session "Recovery Strategy" = `Fail task and continue workflow` (L1000, L4285, L4563);
  - "Stop on errors" 0 (L793);
  - "Rollback Transactions on Errors" NO (L999, L4284, L4562);
  - Command task "Fail task if any command fails" NO (L4059);
  - workflow SUSPEND_ON_ERROR NO (L4054);
  - Pre-SQL TRUNCATE on every target: L535–550, L2389–2401, L3691–3703.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:**
  - An empty link condition means the next task starts whatever the previous task's status.
  - If staging fails after its Pre-SQL truncation, core and enriched still truncate and rebuild the marts from empty or partial STG tables.
  - The workflow is not marked failed.
  - Row-level errors (F06 overflow, F18 NULLs) are dropped without failing anything.
- **Seed impact:** not measurable from a static run.
- **dbt translation:** dbt's DAG stops downstream models on failure, which is a behaviour change worth calling out. Do not try to reproduce "continue on failure".

### F26: Reusable staging session vs workflow task-instance connection overrides
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:**
  - Reusable `s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL` L811–1013: every reader and writer uses `MART_Jaffleshop` (e.g. L888, L900, L912, L961, L965 …).
  - The workflow task instance overrides this (L4579–4619): writers use `STG_Jaffleshop` (L4581, L4584, L4587, L4590, L4593, L4596) and readers use `RAW_Jaffleshop` (L4599 … L4617).
  - Core and enriched (non-reusable) read `STG_Jaffleshop` and write `MART_Jaffleshop`.
  - No table-name-prefix or owner overrides exist, and table names are unqualified, while the Pre-SQL is schema-qualified (`STG.`, `MART.`).
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** task-instance overrides win, so the workflow run behaves correctly. Run on its own, the reusable session would read RAW_* and write STG_* through the MART connection.
- **Seed impact:** none via the workflow.
- **dbt translation:** a converter must resolve connections as task-instance override, then session, then mapping. Map RAW/STG/MART to dbt sources and schemas accordingly.

### F27: Plaintext credential in Command task `cmd_FL_JS_CREATE_RPT_VIEWS`
- **Category:** security. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** TASK L4058–4062 (the credential is on the VALUEPAIR line inside it); task instance L4577; it runs after enriched via L4622, and its failures are ignored (L4059).
- **Evidence:** the task contains a plaintext database credential. Its content is deliberately not reproduced or described here.
- **Impact:** anyone with access to the export (or to the repository it is committed in) has the credential. The reporting views this task creates are not visible to the mappings, so they cannot be checked or converted from the XML.
- **dbt translation:** do not port the command or copy the credential. Treat the credential as compromised and rotate it. If the report views are needed, rebuild them as dbt models (or post-hooks) that use profile-managed credentials.

---

## Intent differences vs jaffle-shop (by design, not defects)
- There is no LOCATIONS mart (only STG_LOCATIONS); jaffle-shop has `locations`.
- ORDERS has HAS_FOOD_ITEMS / HAS_DRINK_ITEMS (MAX of flags) instead of jaffle-shop's `count_food_items`, `count_drink_items`, `count_order_items`, `is_food_order`, `is_drink_order`. ITEMS_COUNT is computed (L3458) but never written.
- STG_SUPPLIES has no `supply_uuid`. STG_PRODUCTS and PRODUCTS add `PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS`.
- The enriched marts (ORDER_ITEM_ENRICHED, ORDER_FINANCIALS, CUSTOMER_360, PRODUCT_DAILY_PERFORMANCE, STORE_DAILY_KPIS) have no jaffle-shop equivalent; their intent was inferred from names and formulas.

## Areas checked and found clean
- **Connector integrity:** every connector references an existing port. No port is fed twice. Every transformation input and every target column is connected. Mapping wiring was checked across all 28 source qualifiers, 25 expressions, 16 joiners, 9 aggregators, 15 sorters, 2 routers, 2 unions and 1 filter (`work/wiring.txt`).
- **String precision:** no string narrowing along any connector or into any target. Seed maximum lengths fit the declared precisions (names ≤ 32, descriptions ≤ 94, ids ≤ 36).
- **Source qualifiers:** none has a SQL override, user-defined join, source filter, sorted ports, Select Distinct or pre/post SQL. No session-level transformation overrides exist.
- **Aggregators:** every output port is either a group-by port or an aggregate. No non-aggregated outputs. Unused inputs (e.g. CUSTOMER_ID at L2012, SUPPLY_ID/SUPPLY_NAME at L3288–3289) are input-only, so harmless. COUNT(*) at L3458 is valid. Sorted Input is NO everywhere, so there is no dependency on sorter output.
- **Sorters:** no Distinct. Only the two sequence expressions (F07, F08) depend on sort order, and their sort keys match their intent. Case-insensitive sorting has no effect on lower-case UUID keys.
- **Joiner keys:** string-to-string everywhere. Case-sensitive comparison matches SQL. The inner (Normal) joins (staging supplies↔products, items↔orders, items↔products) are correct apart from F20.
- **Other expressions:** TRUNC(OPENED_AT) (L234), EFFECTIVE_TAX_RATE and food/drink shares, all ISNULL cleanups and IIF guards against division by zero. There is no integer division anywhere (every division involves a decimal or double).
- **Unions:** both act as UNION ALL, input groups align with their sources via the connectors, and all 19 + 19 (enriched) and 15 (staging) inputs are connected.
- **Filter FIL_LOCS:** correct for what it does (see F11).
- **Target load order** (L762–767, L3099–3103, L4047–4051): the pipelines inside each mapping are independent, so order does not matter. **Pre-SQL truncation plus bulk insert** is a valid full refresh (risk only as in F25).
- **Session date format** (L782) is consistent with the `$$RUN_DATE` default format. There are no mapplets, shortcuts, worklets, lookups, update strategies or sequence generators.

- **Evidence:** the three "previous" variables are set from the current row before the test `IIF(v_PREV_LOCATION = LOCATION_ID AND v_PREV_DAY = ORDERED_AT_DAY AND v_PREV_CUSTOMER = CUSTOMER_ID, 0, 1)`.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** the test is always TRUE, so the flag is 0. The flag is 1 only when one of the keys is NULL.
- **Seed impact:** 538/538 store-days are 0; the intended total is 61,465. SQL: `select sum(u) from (select location_id, ordered_at_day, count(distinct customer_id) u from of_pc group by 1,2);` → 61465.
- **dbt translation:** faithful: `sum(case when location_id is null or ordered_at_day is null or customer_id is null then 1 else 0 end)`. Intended: `count(distinct customer_id)`.

### F09: ORDER_VALUE_BAND threshold applied to cents
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** RTR_ORDER_VALUE_BAND L1738–1816 (L1740 `ORDER_TOTAL >= 50`, L1742 `ORDER_TOTAL < 50`, L1741 DEFAULT1 unconnected); bands set at L1835 and L1857; consumers L2010, L2040, L2195. ORDER_TOTAL comes from L2742 and is in cents (F01).
- **Seed impact:** 61,465 HIGH and 0 STANDARD, where dollars would give 1,216 and 60,249. HIGH_VALUE_ORDERS_PCT is 1.0 on all 538 store-days.
  - SQL: `select count(*) filter (where order_value_band='HIGH'), count(*) filter (where order_value_band='STANDARD') from of_pc;` → 61465, 0. `select count(*) filter (where order_total>=50) from seed.main.orders where order_id in (select order_id from of_pc);` → 1216.
- **dbt translation:** faithful: compare cents with 50. Intended: dollars.

### F10: Orders without items dropped by Master Outer joins
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:**
  - Core JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG L3499–3528: master L3501–3509 plus L3515 (`ORDER_ID1` INPUT/MASTER), L3518 `ORDER_ID1 = ORDER_ID`, L3519 `Master Outer Join`, fed by L3965 (orders) and L3949 (aggregate).
  - Enriched JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG L1573–1600: master L1574–1580, L1590, L1591, fed by L2736 (orders → master ORDER_ID) and L2729 (aggregate → ORDER_ID1).
- **PowerCenter reasoning:**
  - Master Outer keeps every detail row plus the matching master rows. Orders are the master here, so orders with no items are discarded.
  - The author expected them to survive: the ISNULL→0 cleanup ports are L1619–1624 and L3537–3540.
  - jaffle-shop uses `orders left join order_items_summary`.
- **Seed impact:**
  - 483 orders (all $0, 85 customers) are missing from ORDERS (61,465 instead of 61,948) and from ORDER_FINANCIALS.
  - CUSTOMER_360 order counts are lower for 85 customers; F_SCORE changes for 2; first and last order dates each differ for 5.
  - STORE_DAILY_KPIS.ORDERS_COUNT is lower on 319 of 538 store-days, which inflates AVG_ORDER_VALUE. Money totals are unchanged.
  - SQL: `select count(*), sum(order_total), count(distinct customer) from seed.raw.raw_orders o where not exists (select 1 from seed.raw.raw_items i where i.order_id=o.id);` → 483, 0, 85.
- **dbt translation:** faithful: `item_agg LEFT JOIN orders`. In the enriched joiner the output ORDER_ID comes from the master side, so it is NULL when no order matches. Intended: `orders LEFT JOIN item_agg`.

### F11: Master/detail inverted on every Master Outer join
- **Category:** wrong data (latent). **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** Master Outer keeps all detail rows. In every one of these joiners the main stream is the master and the enrichment table is the detail. Joiners never match NULL keys, which partly masks the problem.

| Joiner (lines) | Master | Detail | Actually keeps | Seed effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Core JNR_ADD_SUPPLY_COST L3303–3328 (L3318–3319) | item stream (L3304–3312 /M, L3315 PRODUCT_ID1 MASTER, fed L3868) | supply aggregate (L3306, fed L3893) | all supplied products; items without supplies dropped; an unsold product gives an ORDER_ITEMS row with NULL ids; output PRODUCT_ID comes from the aggregate side | 0 |
| Core JNR_ITEMS_SUPPLIES L3434–3455 (L3445–3446) | item stream | AGG_SUPPLIES_BY_PRODUCT2 (fed L3922) | same pattern; an unsold product gives an ORDERS row with NULL ORDER_ID | 0 |
| Core JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG | orders | item aggregate | see F10 | 483 dropped |
| Core JNR_CUSTOMERS_ORDERS L3651–3673 (L3663–3664) | customers (L3652–3653, fed L4030) | order aggregate (fed L4032) | only customers with orders; CUSTOMER_ID comes from the master side, so it is NULL for orphan orders | 0 |
| Enriched JNR_ADD_CUSTOMERS L1333–1359 (L1349–1350) | item stream | customers (fed L2633) | all customers; items with an unknown customer dropped | 0 |
| Enriched JNR_ADD_LOCATIONS L1378–1407 (L1397–1398) | item stream | locations (fed L2647) | all locations | 90,904 rows out (4 phantoms, dropped by the next joiner) |
| Enriched JNR_ADD_SUPPLIES L1454–1485 (L1475–1476) | item stream | supply aggregate (fed L2672) | all supplied products | 90,900 out |
| Enriched JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG | orders | item aggregate | see F10 | 483 dropped |
| Enriched JNR_ADD_LOCATION_INFO L2061–2090 (L2080–2081) | store-day aggregate (fed L2951) | locations (fed L2969) | all locations; 4 NULL-LOCATION_ID phantoms removed by FIL_LOCS (L2385). Net effect is an inner join | 0 |
| Enriched JNR_CUSTOMERS L2227–2252 (L2242–2243) | customers (L2238 /M, L2239 MASTER, fed L3027) | customer aggregate (fed L3015) | only customers with orders (so PROSPECT is dead, F14) | 0 |

- **dbt translation:** derive join direction from the PORTTYPE MASTER flags plus the join type, never from input order or names. Faithful SQL for Master Outer is `detail LEFT JOIN master`; output columns come from whichever side owns the port. jaffle-shop intends left joins from customers and from items.

### F12: M_SCORE thresholds applied to cents
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** L2343 `IIF(LIFETIME_SPEND>=200,3,IIF(LIFETIME_SPEND>=50,2,1))`; spend comes from L2190 (cents).
- **Seed impact:** M=3 for 935/935, where dollars would give 797/112/26. RFM_SCORE is wrong for the 138 customers under $200. SQL is on `c360_pc` (`spend` vs `spend/100`).
- **dbt translation:** faithful: thresholds on the cents sum.

### F13: $$RUN_DATE fixed default; parameter file missing; workflow variable unused
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** confirmed for the default; effective value unknown.
- **Lines:** L3104 (default `12/31/2025 00:00:00`); used at L2300 and L2318; the parameter file at L4554 (Windows path) is not shipped; `$$wf_run_date` (L4677) is declared and never referenced; variable-assignment components are empty (L4146–4163, L4436–4453).
- **Seed impact:** recency ranges 122–232 days, so R_SCORE=1 for all 935. CHAMPION and LOYAL are unreachable; segments are 929 AT_RISK and 6 STANDARD.
- **dbt translation:** `var('run_date','2025-12-31')`, not `current_date`.

### F14: PROSPECT segment unreachable
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** L2366; L2256 passes the raw count rather than the cleaned `v_ORDERS_CL` (L2267); JNR_CUSTOMERS.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** no-order customers never arrive (F11). Even if one did, `NULL = 0` would fall through to STANDARD with a NULL count. The cleanups at L2267–2273 never fire.
- **Seed impact:** 0.
- **dbt translation:** keep the logic as written but document it as dead code.

### F15: IS_PERISHABLE accepts only 'Y'/'1'
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** likely.
- **Lines:** source L10 (varchar2(50)); L504 `IIF(PERISHABLE = 'Y' OR PERISHABLE = '1', 1, 0)`; aggregated at L1444 and L3292; consumers L1507, L2159, L3340.
- **Evidence:** the seed CSV stores True/False. Loaded as text into varchar2, the column holds 'True'/'False', which never match (the comparison is exact and case-sensitive).
- **Seed impact:** 0 of 65 supplies flagged where 30 should be. HAS_PERISHABLE_SUPPLY is 0 for all 10 products and all 90,900 items, though every product actually has a perishable supply.
- **dbt translation:** faithful: compare on the same text the Oracle table holds; casting the boolean seed differently silently changes the result. Intended: pass the boolean through.

### F16: Scale-0 decimal ports on money
- **Category:** misleading/latent. **Confidence:** speculative (impact).
- **Lines:** L3382 decimal(10,0) → L3441 → L3465 (12,0) → L3459–3460 (12,0) → L3537–3538 → ORDERS NUMBER(12,2); L2009 (12,0) → L2036; L116 (12,0). The sibling aggregator is (12,2) at L3291. High precision is NO in all sessions (L1007, L4292, L4570).
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** with high precision off, decimals are processed as double. I expect the scale not to be applied, but I can't prove it from the XML. With high precision on, these ports round.
- **Seed impact:** with no rounding, ORDER_COST matches jaffle-shop exactly (0 diffs). With rounding, 61,377/61,465 orders change and the total becomes 151,444 instead of 131,788.38; GROSS_PROFIT_TOTAL changes on 538 store-days.
- **dbt translation:** record the assumption (treat as double).

### F17: ORDERED_AT_DAY via 'DD-MM-YY'
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** likely.
- **Lines:** L110 `TO_DATE(TO_CHAR(ORDERED_AT, 'DD-MM-YY'), 'DD-MM-YY')`.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** the round trip truncates to the day. YY assumes the current century, so pre-2000 dates would shift. TRUNC (as at L234) would be safer.
- **Seed impact:** 0 of 61,948.
- **dbt translation:** `date_trunc('day', ordered_at)`.

### F18: ERROR() defaults on I/O ports; output-port defaults
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** likely.
- **Lines:** L235 TAX_RATE (I/O, `ERROR('Transformation Error')`); L455 ORDER_ID (I/O, same); L503 and L504 (OUTPUT, default '0'); L793 Stop on errors 0. Every other I/O port has an empty default.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** a NULL input to those I/O ports skips the row with a row error and no failure. Output-port defaults apply only to expression errors, not to NULLs.
- **Seed impact:** 0.
- **dbt translation:** filter `tax_rate is not null` and `order_id is not null`. Do not coalesce for the output defaults.

### F19: REGION bands, no-op chain, suffix traps
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** L236; sorters, router, rename expressions and union at L242–452 (router groups L276–279, default L277 and outputs L300–304 unconnected; G_APAC has a trailing CR/LF).
- **Seed impact:** all 6 stores are AMER; the APAC and EMEA paths are empty.
- **Converter trap:** the router's `*2` ports are DEFAULT while the union's `*2` ports are APAC; the enriched mapping repeats this (L1797–1814 vs L1884–1902). Follow connectors, not names.
- **dbt translation:** a single CASE expression.

### F20: Staging supplies inner-joined to products
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** L479–498 (L488–489, master L485 fed L756).
- **Seed impact:** 0 dropped; 29 distinct supply ids across 65 rows, and there is no supply_uuid.
- **dbt translation:** an inner join; no uniqueness test on supply_id.

### F21: Food/drink flags case-insensitive and trimmed
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** L204–205.
- **Seed impact:** 0.
- **dbt translation:** `upper(trim(type))`.

### F22: NULL ORDER_TOTAL goes to the unconnected router default
- **Category:** harmless. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** L1741, L1797–1814. The two conditions do not overlap and leave no gap apart from NULL.
- **Seed impact:** 0.
- **dbt translation:** filter out NULL totals before banding.

### F23: Duplicated logic
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Evidence:**
  - core AGG_SUPPLIES_BY_PRODUCT L3287–3302 vs AGG_SUPPLIES_BY_PRODUCT2 L3380–3391;
  - core ORDERS rebuilds its own item pipeline (L3345–3455) instead of aggregating ORDER_ITEMS;
  - EXP_RECENCY1 L2300 duplicates EXP_RECENCY2 L2318, and RECENCY_DAYS_TEMP (L2319) is unused;
  - staging tables are read 2–3 times each.

### F24: Core vs enriched inconsistencies
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Order amounts:** ORDERS = raw ÷ 10,000 (L3534–3536) vs ORDER_FINANCIALS = cents (L2740–2742), a factor of 10,000.
- **Lifetime spend:** CUSTOMERS holds the cents total (L3636); CUSTOMER_360.LIFETIME_SPEND holds tax in cents (F05). Differs for 935 customers.
- **Lifetime order counts:** CUSTOMERS counts all orders (L4022–4027); CUSTOMER_360 counts only orders with items. Differs for 85 customers.
- **First/last dates:** L3634–3635 vs L2188–2189; 5 customers differ on each.
- **Supply cost:** (12,2) at L3291 and L1443 vs (10,0) at L3382; equal unless the scale is applied.
- **Margin denominators:** ITEM_REVENUE (L1613) vs SUBTOTAL_TOTAL (L2038) vs REVENUE (L2182); equal on the seed.
- **CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUMBER:** identical in both marts, and wrong in both (F07).

### F25: Unconditional links, swallowed failures
- **Category:** wrong data (operational). **Confidence:** configuration confirmed; impact speculative.
- **Lines:**
  - L4622–4625 (`CONDITION =""`);
  - task instances L4577, L4579, L4620, L4621 with `FAIL_PARENT_IF_INSTANCE_FAILS ="NO"`;
  - recovery "Fail task and continue workflow" at L1000, L4285, L4563;
  - Stop on errors 0 (L793); Rollback on errors NO (L999, L4284, L4562);
  - command task "Fail task if any command fails" NO (L4059); SUSPEND_ON_ERROR NO (L4054);
  - Pre-SQL TRUNCATE at L535–550, L2389–2401, L3691–3703.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** an empty link condition runs the next task whatever happened before. If staging fails after its truncation, the marts are still rebuilt from empty or partial staging tables, and the workflow isn't marked failed.
- **dbt translation:** dbt stops downstream models on failure, which is a behaviour change worth noting.

### F26: Reusable session connections
- **Category:** misleading-but-works. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** the reusable `s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL` (L811–1013) uses MART_Jaffleshop for all readers and writers (L888, L900, L912, L961, …). The task instance (L4579–4619) overrides writers to STG_Jaffleshop (L4581–4596) and readers to RAW_Jaffleshop (L4599–4617). There are no table-name-prefix or owner overrides; table names are unqualified while the Pre-SQL is schema-qualified.
- **dbt translation:** resolve connections as task-instance override, then session, then mapping.

### F27: Plaintext credential in Command task
- **Category:** security. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** TASK `cmd_FL_JS_CREATE_RPT_VIEWS` L4058–4062; instance L4577; runs after enriched via L4622; failures ignored (L4059).
- **Evidence:** the task contains a plaintext database credential. Its content is not reproduced or described here.
- **dbt translation:** don't port it; rotate the credential; rebuild any report views as dbt models using profile-managed credentials.

## Intent differences vs jaffle-shop (by design)
- No LOCATIONS mart.
- ORDERS has HAS_FOOD/HAS_DRINK instead of the count columns and is_*_order flags; ITEMS_COUNT (L3458) is computed but never written.
- No supply_uuid; an extra PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS column.
- The enriched marts have no jaffle-shop equivalent; their intent was inferred from names and formulas.

## Areas checked and found clean
- **Connectors:** every connector references an existing port; no port is fed twice; every transformation input and target column is connected (checked across 28 SQs, 25 expressions, 16 joiners, 9 aggregators, 15 sorters, 2 routers, 2 unions, 1 filter).
- **Strings:** no narrowing anywhere, and seed lengths fit.
- **Source qualifiers:** no SQL override, user join, filter, sorted ports, Distinct or pre/post SQL; no session-level overrides.
- **Aggregators:** every output is grouped or aggregated; unused inputs are input-only; COUNT(*) is valid; Sorted Input is NO everywhere.
- **Sorters:** no Distinct; only F07 and F08 depend on order, and their keys match intent.
- **Joiner keys:** string-to-string and case-sensitive; Normal joins are fine apart from F20.
- **Expressions:** TRUNC(OPENED_AT), EFFECTIVE_TAX_RATE, the food/drink shares, ISNULL cleanups and divide-by-zero guards are correct; there is no integer division.
- **Unions:** UNION ALL semantics, groups aligned with their inputs, all inputs connected.
- **Filter:** FIL_LOCS is correct for what it does.
- **Run order and refresh:** target load order is harmless because the pipelines are independent; Pre-SQL truncate plus bulk insert is a valid full refresh (risk only as in F25).
- **Other:** the date format (L782) is consistent with the $$RUN_DATE default; there are no mapplets, shortcuts, worklets, lookups, update strategies or sequence generators.

I didn't open docs/, agent_log.md, the other scratchpad scripts or any transcript. Every line number below was checked against the raw XML.

## Compact findings list
1. **F01 STG_ORDERS columns cross-wired** (L608–613, from EXP_ORDERS L111–116): the `*_CENTS` columns hold dollars and `SUBTOTAL`/`TAX_PAID`/`ORDER_TOTAL` hold cents. Changed values in 61,465 of 61,948 rows; the other 483 are $0 orders. Every downstream amount inherits it. Confirmed.
2. **F02 STG_PRODUCTS price cross-wired** (L620–621, from L201–202): `PRODUCT_PRICE` holds cents. Affects all 10 products, and through them all 90,900 ORDER_ITEMS prices and ORDERS.ORDER_ITEMS_SUBTOTAL (100×). Confirmed.
3. **F03 Core ORDERS divides by 100 again** (L3534–3536) using the `*_CENTS` columns, which already hold dollars. SUBTOTAL/TAX/TOTAL come out 100× too small (overall raw ÷ 10,000) on all 61,465 rows; max ORDER_TOTAL is 1.05 instead of 104.94. One ORDERS row now mixes three units. Confirmed.
4. **F04 Revenue in cents minus cost in dollars** (L1501–1506/L1513, L1610–1613, L2156–2158/L2182, L2005–2009/L2038). Every gross-profit and margin figure is wrong: item margin averages 0.998 instead of 0.793. Confirmed.
5. **F05 CUSTOMER_360 spend columns rotated** (L2480–2482): SPEND→PRETAX, PRETAX→TAX, TAX→SPEND. All 935 rows. Confirmed.
6. **F06 PRODUCT_DAILY_PERFORMANCE MARGIN_PCT and PERISHABLE_SALES_FLAG swapped** (L2542–2543). The margin is also rounded into a NUMBER(1,0) column (L1087). All 3,635 rows: MARGIN_PCT = 0, flag = 1. Confirmed.
7. **F07 CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUMBER is a global running count** (core L3588–3590, enriched L1704–1706). The "previous customer" variable is overwritten with the current customer before the comparison, so the count never resets: 1…61,465, with 61,275 rows different from per-customer numbering. Confirmed.
8. **F08 UNIQUE_CUSTOMERS is always 0** (L2124–2127, L2004). Same port-order bug; 538 of 538 store-days are 0, where the intended total is 61,465. Confirmed.
9. **F09 ORDER_VALUE_BAND compares 50 against cents** (L1740/L1742 on data from L2742). Every order is HIGH (61,465 HIGH, 0 STANDARD) where dollars would give 1,216 HIGH; HIGH_VALUE_ORDERS_PCT is 1.0 everywhere. Confirmed.
10. **F10 Orders without items are dropped** by Master Outer joins with orders as the master (core L3499–3528, enriched L1573–1600). 483 orders are missing from ORDERS and ORDER_FINANCIALS, which also skews CUSTOMER_360 for 85 customers and STORE_DAILY_KPIS order counts on 319 store-days. The ISNULL cleanup ports show the author expected these orders to survive. Confirmed.
11. **F11 Master and detail are reversed on all 10 Master Outer joiners** (table in appendix). Each keeps the lookup side instead of the main stream, which is the reverse of a left join. On the seed the only effect is F10 (4 phantom rows appear but are removed downstream). Real data would lose customers without orders and items without supplies, and produce rows with NULL IDs. Confirmed semantics; latent.
12. **F12 M_SCORE thresholds compared against cents** (L2343): M = 3 for all 935 customers instead of 797/112/26. Confirmed.
13. **F13 $$RUN_DATE is fixed at 2025-12-31** (L3104). The parameter file named at L4554 isn't in the export and `$$wf_run_date` (L4677) is never used. With the default, R_SCORE = 1 for everyone (recency 122–232 days); segments come out 929 AT_RISK and 6 STANDARD. The default is confirmed; the value used at run time is unknown.
14. **F14 PROSPECT segment can never be assigned** (L2366, L2256): no-order customers are dropped by JNR_CUSTOMERS, and the order count is NULL rather than 0 anyway. Confirmed.
15. **F15 IS_PERISHABLE only accepts 'Y' or '1'** (L504), but the source column is varchar2 (L10) and the seed CSV holds True/False. If it was loaded as text, all 65 supplies, 10 products and 90,900 items get 0, where 30 supplies should be 1. Likely; depends on how Oracle was loaded.
16. **F16 Money in scale-0 decimal ports** (L3382, L3459–3460, L3465, L2009, L116), with "Enable high precision" = NO (L1007, L4292, L4570). If the scale is not applied, there is no seed impact. If it is applied, 61,377 orders change and ORDER_COST totals 151,444 instead of 131,788.38. Speculative impact.
17. **F17 ORDERED_AT_DAY via TO_CHAR/TO_DATE with a two-digit year** (L110). Truncates to the day correctly; years outside the current century would shift. 0 seed rows affected. Likely.
18. **F18 ERROR() defaults on two input/output ports** (L235 TAX_RATE, L455 ORDER_ID) silently drop rows with NULLs. Separately, the '0' defaults at L503–504 do not replace NULLs. 0 seed rows. Likely.
19. **F19 REGION is derived from tax-rate bands** (L236): all 6 stores are AMER, the router/sorter/union chain does nothing, and port-number suffixes don't line up between transformations. Harmless.
20. **F20 Staging inner-joins supplies to products** (L488–489) and supply_id isn't unique (29 distinct ids in 65 rows). Harmless on the seed.
21. **F21 Food/drink flags are case-insensitive and trimmed** (L204–205). Harmless.
22. **F22 NULL ORDER_TOTAL rows go to the unconnected router default group and are lost** (L1741, L1797–1814). 0 seed rows; harmless.
23. **F23 Duplicated logic**: two supply aggregators with different precision (L3291 vs L3382), duplicate recency expressions (L2300/L2318), and repeated source reads. Misleading-but-works.
24. **F24 Core and enriched marts disagree**: ORDERS vs ORDER_FINANCIALS amounts differ by 10,000×; CUSTOMERS vs CUSTOMER_360 differ on spend (935 customers), order counts (85) and first/last dates (5 each). Confirmed.
25. **F25 Workflow links have no conditions and failures are swallowed** (L4622–4625, FAIL_PARENT NO, "Fail task and continue workflow", Stop on errors 0, Pre-SQL TRUNCATE). If staging fails, the marts are still rebuilt from truncated or partial staging tables. Configuration confirmed; impact speculative.
26. **F26 Reusable staging session uses MART_Jaffleshop** (L888 etc.); only the workflow task instance points it at RAW_/STG_ (L4579–4619). Works when run through the workflow; a converter must apply the task-instance override.
27. **F27 Command task `cmd_FL_JS_CREATE_RPT_VIEWS` (L4058–4062) contains a plaintext database credential.** Security. Don't port it; rotate the credential.

## Clean areas
Every connector points at an existing port, no port is fed twice, and every transformation input and target column is connected. No string is narrowed along the way, and seed values fit the declared lengths. No source qualifier has an SQL override, filter, Distinct or sorted ports, and no session overrides any transformation. Every aggregator output is either grouped or aggregated. Sorters use no Distinct, and the only logic that depends on sort order (F07, F08) is sorted on the right keys. Joiner keys are string-to-string and case-sensitive. The Normal joins are fine apart from F20. There is no integer division, and ratio metrics that don't involve cost (EFFECTIVE_TAX_RATE, food/drink shares) are correct. Both unions line up correctly with their inputs. Target load order is harmless because the pipelines are independent. The session date format matches the `$$RUN_DATE` default. There are no lookups, mapplets, update strategies or sequence generators.

# Blind review: FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml

Independent, from-scratch review of `external/flowline-pwc-demo/FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml` (4,701 lines) before writing a PowerCenter-to-dbt converter.

## How this was done
- **XML.** Read through a redacting parser (VALUEPAIR attributes dropped). The compact dumps and wiring checks are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-junaidatique--claude-spares-spare-x2tKTE/df021aa3-23ff-4dbf-a7c9-3e227d3a8b25/scratchpad/review/blind/work/` (`maps.txt`, `wiring.txt`, `outline.txt`). Every line number below was checked against the raw file. "L" means physical line in the XML.
- **Intent.** dbt-labs/jaffle-shop models. The jaffle-shop dbt outputs already built in the same DuckDB file (`main.orders`, `main.customers`, `main.order_items`, …) serve as the "intended" values.
- **Data impact.** I simulated what PowerCenter would actually do on the seed (`raw.*`). The view definitions are in `work/sim.sql`; `work/run.py` attaches the seed read-only and runs them; the raw query output is in `work/impact1.txt`…`impact4.txt`. The simulation follows PowerCenter semantics: joiner master/detail roles, port order, the unconnected router default group, and the 'True'/'False' text the source DDL implies for `PERISHABLE`.
- **Seed facts used throughout.** 935 customers (all have orders), 61,948 orders (2024-09-01 to 2025-08-31), 483 of those orders have no items (all with subtotal/tax/total 0, belonging to 85 customers), 90,900 items, 10 products (all sold, all supplied), 65 supply rows (29 distinct supply ids), 6 stores (only Philadelphia and Brooklyn have orders).

Categories: wrong data / misleading-but-works / harmless / security. Confidence: confirmed / likely / speculative.

### F01: STG_ORDERS cents and dollars columns cross-wired
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** EXP_ORDERS L106–125 (L111–116); connectors L608–613; STG_ORDERS target L67–78.
- **Evidence:**
  - EXP_ORDERS: `SUBTOTAL`=`SUBTOTAL_IN/100` (L111), `SUBTOTAL_CENTS`=`SUBTOTAL_IN` (L114), and the same pattern for TAX_PAID (L112/L115) and ORDER_TOTAL (L113/L116).
  - The connectors then cross them: L608 `SRT_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL -> STG_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL_CENTS`, L609 `TAX_PAID -> TAX_PAID_CENTS`, L610 `ORDER_TOTAL -> ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS`, L611 `SUBTOTAL_CENTS -> SUBTOTAL`, L612 `TAX_PAID_CENTS -> TAX_PAID`, L613 `ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS -> ORDER_TOTAL`.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:** connectors are explicit, by name. So `STG_ORDERS.*_CENTS` hold dollars and `SUBTOTAL/TAX_PAID/ORDER_TOTAL` hold cents.
- **Downstream:** core CUSTOMERS reads cents via SQ_STG_ORDERS2 (L4025–4027 → L3636–3638). Enriched ORDER_FINANCIALS reads cents via SQ_STG_ORDERS1 (L2740–2742 → L1606–1608), and CUSTOMER_360 and STORE_DAILY_KPIS aggregate that stream. Core ORDERS reads the `*_CENTS` columns instead (F03).
- **Seed impact:**
  - 61,465/61,948 rows carry swapped values; the other 483 are $0 orders. Sample: order 0004b076… gets SUBTOTAL_CENTS=5.0 and SUBTOTAL=500.0.
  - CUSTOMERS lifetime spend is exactly 100× jaffle-shop for 935/935 customers.
  - STORE_DAILY_KPIS revenue totals 67,142,537 (cents) instead of $671,425.37.
  - SQL: `select count(*), count(*) filter (where subtotal_cents_col<>subtotal_col), count(*) filter (where order_total_cents_col<>order_total_col) from stg_orders_pc;` → 61948, 61465, 61465. `select count(*) filter (where p.lifetime_spend <> j.lifetime_spend*100) from core_customers_pc p join seed.main.customers j using(customer_id);` → 0.
- **dbt translation:** a faithful port writes `subtotal_cents = raw/100.0` and `subtotal = raw cents` (likewise tax and total). The intended model is jaffle-shop `stg_orders`. Decide explicitly which one you want; fixing this changes F03, F09 and F12.

### F07: CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUMBER is a global running number
- **Category:** wrong data. **Confidence:** confirmed.
- **Lines:** enriched L1686–1708 (L1705 `v_PREV_CUSTOMER_ID`=`CUSTOMER_ID`, L1706 `v_ORDER_SEQUENCE`=`IIF(v_PREV_CUSTOMER_ID = CUSTOMER_ID, v_ORDER_SEQUENCE + 1, 1)`, L1704 output); core L3576–3592 (L3588–3590). Sorters L1635–1662 and L3554–3575.
- **PowerCenter reasoning:**
  - PowerCenter evaluates input ports, then variable ports top to bottom, then outputs.
  - The "previous customer" variable is overwritten with the current customer before the comparison, so the comparison is always TRUE for a non-NULL customer. The sequence counts 1…N over the whole session.
  - A NULL customer makes the comparison NULL, IIF falls to 1, and counting restarts.
- **Seed impact:** both marts number 1…61,465. Only 190 rows match jaffle-shop's `row_number() over (partition by customer_id order by ordered_at)`; 61,275 differ. Max is 61,465 instead of 231.
  - SQL: `select count(*), count(*) filter (where p.customer_order_number=j.customer_order_number), max(p.customer_order_number), max(j.customer_order_number) from core_orders_pc p join seed.main.orders j using(order_id);` → 61465, 190, 61465, 231.
- **dbt translation:**
  - Faithful: a global `row_number() over (order by customer_id, ordered_at_day, order_id)` over the post-join rows only.
  - The sorters are case-insensitive (L1654, L3567).
  - NULL placement differs: core has Null Treated Low YES (L3571), enriched NO (L1658).
  - Reset after a NULL customer.
  - Intended: partition by customer.

## Intent differences vs jaffle-shop (by design)
- No LOCATIONS mart.
- ORDERS has HAS_FOOD/HAS_DRINK instead of the count columns and is_*_order flags; ITEMS_COUNT (L3458) is computed but never written.
- No supply_uuid; an extra PRODUCT_PRICE_CENTS column.
- The enriched marts have no jaffle-shop equivalent; their intent was inferred from names and formulas.

## Areas checked and found clean
- **Connectors:** every connector references an existing port; no port is fed twice; every transformation input and target column is connected (checked across 28 SQs, 25 expressions, 16 joiners, 9 aggregators, 15 sorters, 2 routers, 2 unions, 1 filter).
- **Strings:** no narrowing anywhere, and seed lengths fit.
- **Source qualifiers:** no SQL override, user join, filter, sorted ports, Distinct or pre/post SQL; no session-level overrides.
- **Aggregators:** every output is grouped or aggregated; unused inputs are input-only; COUNT(*) is valid; Sorted Input is NO everywhere.
- **Sorters:** no Distinct; only F07 and F08 depend on order, and their keys match intent.
- **Joiner keys:** string-to-string and case-sensitive; Normal joins are fine apart from F20.
- **Expressions:** TRUNC(OPENED_AT), EFFECTIVE_TAX_RATE, the food/drink shares, ISNULL cleanups and divide-by-zero guards are correct; there is no integer division.
- **Unions:** UNION ALL semantics, groups aligned with their inputs, all inputs connected.
- **Filter:** FIL_LOCS is correct for what it does.
- **Run order and refresh:** target load order is harmless because the pipelines are independent; Pre-SQL truncate plus bulk insert is a valid full refresh (risk only as in F25).
- **Other:** the date format (L782) is consistent with the $$RUN_DATE default; there are no mapplets, shortcuts, worklets, lookups, update strategies or sequence generators.
